chapters.headline: Reply to Mr. Stewart, of Pennsylvania
chapters.text:
Reply to Mr. Stewart, of Pennsylvania. House of Representatives, January 17 and 18, 1844.
(ALTO of the heading dates is 1811 / 1841 in places.) Tuesday 16 January: Stewart concluded; Weller obtained the floor. Wednesday 17: Weller, after a night's reflection, had no disposition to make a long speech. History of the debate: Mr. Thomasson of Kentucky, resolution to keep the snag-boats on the western waters; Messrs. Wilkins, Bowlin; then Stewart's stump speech covering party politics while news arrived of a Mississippi steamboat striking a snag (fifty to seventy-five lives). Weller moved the previous question. Afternoon: Stewart personal explanation; Van Buren and the Cumberland road estimates. Thursday 18: Stewart an hour in committee; "I have fixed the brand of falsehood on the brow of the member from Ohio." Weller: he will tomorrow "answer a fool according to his folly." Friday 19: Weller's full reply begins and runs onto page 2.

chapters.headline: Clay's Opinion of White Slavery
chapters.text: Clay's Opinion of White Slavery. From Clays Speech in 1819. If gentlemen will not allow us to have black slaves, they must let us white ones; for we cannot cut our own firewood and black our shoes, and have our wives and daughters work in the kitchen. Whig sheets deny the authenticity. Niles Register, 16th volume, page 67: Monday, 15 February 1819, Missouri bill; Clay opposed Talmadge proviso. The page of the Intelligencer containing that speech torn from the Congressional files. Secondary proof from Mr. Taylor of New York (20 March 1819) and a note to Mr. Rich of Vermont.
